subject: Typography
label: WEBSITE TYPOGRAPHY
caption_ig:
If reading your site feels like hard work, mobile visitors won't stay. Ultra-thin fonts and light grey text look great in a desktop mockup, but in daylight on a phone, they become unreadable.

Open your site on your phone right now. Can you comfortably read it at arm's length?

#webdesign #smallbusinesswebsite #userexperience #conversionrate #typography
caption_fb:
One of the most common issues on small business websites is typography choice. Many owners pick light or thin font styles expecting a clean, modern feel. While that can look sharp on a large desktop monitor, it usually breaks down on a smartphone.

When text is thin or low-contrast, it forces visitors to strain their eyes. The moment reading feels like physical effort, potential clients simply leave. Stick to regular font weights, a 16px minimum font size, and high-contrast dark charcoal text so your core message is effortless to absorb.
caption_li:
Unreadable typography is a quiet conversion killer for mobile websites.

It is common for business owners to approve ultra-light font weights in design mockups because they look minimal on a high-resolution screen.

However, mobile users browsing on the move struggle with thin, low-contrast text. If reading your value proposition requires effort, user drop-off increases.

Three simple technical adjustments fix this:
1. Increase paragraph body text to 16px minimum.
2. Use regular font weight (400) instead of light (300).
3. Set body text to high-contrast dark charcoal.

Good design makes reading effortless. When did you last audit your site's readability on a mobile device?

slides.title: Hold your phone at arm’s length right now.
slides.body: Open your website homepage on your phone. If your body text becomes a grey blur at arm's length, mobile visitors aren't reading your offer—they are leaving.

slides.title: Ultra-thin fonts look modern on desktop, invisible on mobile.
slides.body: Light font weights look sleek on a designer's big monitor. But outside in daylight, thin, pale grey lettering disappears entirely on a smartphone screen.

slides.title: 16px is the absolute minimum for mobile text.
slides.body: Anything smaller forces users to pinch, zoom, or strain. If a prospect has to work to read your services or pricing, they close the tab.

slides.title: Swap light grey for dark charcoal (#222222).
slides.body: Pure black text can feel harsh, but light grey causes eye strain. High-contrast dark charcoal keeps text sharp, solid, and easy to scan on small screens.

slides.title: Give your web developer these 3 quick fixes:
slides.body:
1. Set paragraph text to 16px minimum.
2. Upgrade font weight to Regular (400).
3. Use high-contrast dark charcoal on light backgrounds.
Then re-test on your phone.
